Set a narrow research question

Competitor research becomes vague when the request is simply to "analyze the market." Name the companies, product editions, geography if relevant, and decision the update should inform. A useful question might be whether three named products changed how they describe Slack collaboration since the last sales guide.

Give Maia the team's previous approved snapshot if one exists. This creates a clear baseline and keeps the output focused on changes rather than repeating a full profile every week.

Use sources a reviewer can open

Ask Maia to start with official product documentation, release notes, help pages, and pricing pages. Every factual entry should include the page title, link, and date checked. If a page does not establish availability or plan packaging, the digest should say that the detail remains unconfirmed.

Third-party commentary may reveal a question worth checking, but it should not replace the vendor's current documentation for a product claim. Similar company names also need care. The digest should confirm the entity and exact product before comparing it with Maia.

Separate facts from interpretation

A vendor adding a new page is a fact. "They are moving upmarket" is an interpretation that needs more support. Maia can place observed changes in one section and possible implications in another. This lets marketing discuss the interpretation without turning it into a public claim.

The update should also acknowledge overlap. If another product supports shared work in Slack, say so. A fair comparison helps a buyer understand fit and gives sales a better basis for discovery questions.

Turn research into useful questions

The best result is not a long feature grid. Ask Maia to draft questions that sales or marketing can test, such as which work surface the buyer prefers, who configures access, and what output needs approval. These questions connect product research to an actual evaluation.

Review the digest in Slack. A product owner can correct Maia's own capability description, and sales can add what buyers are asking. Keep opinions clearly labelled when the update moves into a brief or campaign.

Begin with one category

Choose two or three direct alternatives and one workflow. Record the official sources, checked date, and unresolved questions. Repeat the same review later to see whether it catches meaningful changes. Do not turn a missing documentation detail into an absent-feature claim.

Questions from marketing teams

How current is the research?

Each brief should state when its sources were checked. Schedule a refresh based on how often the category changes and before using the material in a major launch.

Can Maia compare pricing?

It can summarize public pricing pages when the edition, currency, billing period, and usage terms are clear. A buyer should verify the live quote and total operating assumptions.

Does a changed web page prove a strategy change?

No. It proves only the observed page change. Keep strategic interpretation separate and name the additional evidence needed.
